Wording verified but temporally corrected: the quoted paragraph (a) is the text substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024 s.2(2)(a). At the date of Deed No. 234 (2015) and at 2020-04 section 2 required the writing to be signed by the party in the presence of a licensed notary and two or more witnesses and attested by them; the substance relied on, that a transfer of immovable property must be by a notarially attested deed, held then, the quoted words did not.

Temporal correction: triplicate is the word substituted by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 30 of 2022 s.5. At 2020-04 section 16 read in duplicate. The background point (original, duplicate and protocol) survives, but the Q03 rule statement that deeds are executed in triplicate under s.16 is anachronistic for this matter.

Section 554X sits in the FOREIGN PROBATES chapter (ss.554U-554BB) and, with the interpretation in s.554BB, applies to probate or letters of administration granted by a foreign court and resealed in Sri Lanka. It does not govern the grant made by the District Court in Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T, so it does not support the proposition for which it was cited.

added_provisions.reason: Civil Procedure Code s.545 replaces the rejected s.554X as the authority that makes the testamentary-case documents necessary: no transfer may be effected of property in the estate of a person who died within the preceding five years unless letters of administration or certificates of heirship have issued. Sunil Peiris died on 6 December 2016, so a conveyance at 2020-04 is inside that window. Added as indispensable to M068-Q03.

Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.36 is the provision M068-Q02's authority_requirement_reason turns on (Roman-Dutch law governs only where the Ordinance is silent) but no provision entry carried it. Added as background to M068-Q02 so the statute_only classification rests on a recorded, checked provision.

question_decisions.note: Block confirmed. `acts` shows no Partition Law or Partition Ordinance in the frozen corpus, and no enactment in it supplies the good root of title standard. The nearest candidate, Civil Procedure Code s.207, makes a matter res adjudicata between the same parties only and does not make a partition decree conclusive against the world, so it does not close the gap; it was not added. The devolution limb (ss.21, 22, 25, 27 of 15-1876) verifies. PROV-M068-019 was dropped from the supporting set.

Kept as proposed_gold. Every step is traceable to text: s.22 (widow one-half), s.25 (surviving mother one-half of the balance; full siblings and paternal half-blood take the other half; Keerthi Perera excluded as related only through the surviving parent), s.27 final limb (full siblings take one-half of the collateral portion first, then divide the rest with the one-sided half-blood) and s.30 (per capita). The arithmetic checks and exhausts the whole: 1/2 + 1/4 + 3/32 + 3/32 + 1/32 + 1/32 = 1. Statute_only stands because s.36 makes Roman-Dutch law residual and the Ordinance is not silent on any step.

Downgraded. The gold answer's rule and application rely on Civil Procedure Code s.554X, a foreign-probate resealing provision that does not apply to a Sri Lankan grant, and state that notarial deeds are executed in triplicate under Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.16, which is the 2022 wording and not the text in force at 2020-04. The verifier may not rewrite the answer prose, so the question goes to a lawyer with PROV-M068-901 (CPC s.545) added as the correct hook for the third document class.

disagreements.researcher_position: Civil Procedure Code s.554X shows that a sealed duplicate or certified copy of the letters of administration issued in District Court Testamentary Case No. 345/16/T may be relied on in place of the original.
disagreements.verifier_position: s.554X is in the FOREIGN PROBATES chapter (ss.554U-554BB); with the interpretation in s.554BB it governs only probate or letters of administration granted by a foreign court and resealed in Sri Lanka. It says nothing about a domestic District Court grant. Civil Procedure Code s.545 is the provision that makes the grant or certificates of heirship a document the purchaser must see.

disagreements.researcher_position: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.16 is cited for the proposition that notarial deeds are executed in triplicate, flagged only as amended in 2022 and used as background.
disagreements.verifier_position: The word triplicate was substituted by Act No. 30 of 2022 s.5; at 2020-04 the section read in duplicate. The Q03 rule paragraph states the post-matter-date rule as if it applied to this matter, which is a temporal error in the gold prose, not merely a background flag.

disagreements.researcher_position: Section 27's one-side limb applies to the collateral half created by s.25, giving Kanthi 3/32, Manel 3/32, Upul 1/32 and Wimal 1/32.
disagreements.verifier_position: The verifier accepts this reading, since s.25 admits only the paternal half-blood where the mother survives and s.27's final limb is expressly written for half-siblings of one side. But s.27 sits immediately after s.26 (both parents failing), and a reading that treats the s.25 collateral half as divided equally per capita among all four siblings (1/16 each) is arguable and would change every fraction. The point is flagged rather than resolved.

2-1889/s545 (no transfer without probate, letters of administration or certificates of heirship within five years of the death) was missing altogether and is the strongest statutory hook for the testamentary-case documents in Q03. Added as PROV-M068-901.

Kandyan, Thesawalamai and Muslim personal-law alternatives were re-checked in `acts`: the Kandyan Succession Ordinance, the Jaffna Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance and the Muslim Intestate Succession Ordinance are all in the corpus, and nothing in the facts brings the Peiris family under any of them. The researcher's rejection of them stands.
case_law_dependence: M068-Q01: the good root of title standard and the conclusiveness of a partition final decree are conveyancing practice and judicial authority. The Partition Law is not in the corpus and Civil Procedure Code s.207 gives res adjudicata between the same parties only, not conclusiveness against the world. The block stands and mixed_statute_and_case is the right classification.

M068-Q03: choosing and ordering four classes of document is conveyancing practice rather than statute, though each document's legal effect has a statutory hook. This does not make the question case-dependent, but it is part of why it now goes to a lawyer.
No answer in the map cites a decided case.
enrichment_issues: All three questions are classified keep and enrichment.applied is false with no added facts, which matches the candidate file. Nothing to check for leakage.

PROV-M068-019 is now referenced by no question (it survives in the provisions array marked rejected because claims still cite it), which the validator reports as a warning, not an error.

lawyer_questions: Does section 27's final limb govern the collateral half created by section 25 where half-siblings exist on both sides but only the paternal ones qualify under section 25? On the researcher's reading the shares are Kanthi 3/32, Manel 3/32, Upul 1/32, Wimal 1/32; on an equal per capita reading they are 1/16 each. Every number in M068-Q02 turns on this.
Is any provision in the frozen corpus capable of carrying the conclusiveness of a partition final decree, or must M068-Q01 stay blocked until the Partition Law is added?

For M068-Q03, should the third document class be re-drafted on Civil Procedure Code s.545 (and s.531) rather than s.554X, and should the triplicate sentence be corrected to the duplicate rule in force at 2020-04?

Deed No. 234 conveyed an undivided one-third share of the road reservation Lot R. No enactment in the corpus governs road reservations created on a private sub-division, so the nature of that share and whether it passes with Lot B were not tested against statute.
